digest.component_or_area: reconciler committed .bridge_state cache and tickets-store repository growth
propositions: The committed .bridge_state cache in bindings.json (18 MB, 1509 bindings) grows ~12.79 KB per version due to scattered edits of non-read bookkeeping fields (baseline_advanced_at changed 1144 times per pass, last_get_pass 20 times) that defeat git delta compression, comprising 92% of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch.

Deleting the timestamp baseline_advanced_at and moving last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping to a separate get_rotation.json file reduces marginal packed cost per version to ~1.74 KB (7.4x improvement) and halves version growth by eliminating scattered edits.

A stock git fast-export filter pipeline can reclaim ~1.1 GiB of existing history while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges, reducing the branch to 98 MB with byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add of current .bridge_state files.
The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners so .bridge_state must remain committed to git; the solution keeps it on-branch but cheap via content and churn reduction rather than relocation.

Rollout requires mixed-version compatibility: A2-1 writes both legacy and new formats; A2-2 stops legacy writes but reads max(new, legacy) with self-healing; changes are reversible until the reclaim commit introduces a store-epoch guard.

Publication gates include operator-attested descendant workflow execution, explicit host-runtime epoch-refusal probes under quiescence, off-repo backup bundle verification, and zero active sessions/MCP servers stopped confirmation.
